answers.text: Precision after verification is at least 0.8
answers.evidence: Both graders answered false and the consensus mapping keeps that verdict: over the 80 judged (non-tool) findings it gives 39 seeded, 14 real-unseeded and 27 not-a-problem, so precision = (39 + 14) / 80 = 0.66, below 0.8; strict precision = 39 / 80 = 0.49; recall by meaning = 13 / 13 (every defect D01-D13 is matched by at least one finding). Reaching 0.8 would need 11 of the 27 not-a-problem items to be genuine problems, and they are look-and-feel findings (placeholder thumbnails, identity, column alignment, empty space, widows, wrapping) and accessibility best-practice nits (heading levels, landmarks, label-in-name, arrow-key opening).

answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: Both graders answered true: the reply's '## Fix these first' list runs 1-7 from '"Reserve this tool" doesn't actually reserve anything' ('All three raters gave this the top severity') through the stuck basket, the twice-asked date, the double submit, the dark-mode contrast and the sticky bar down to 'The tool list on phones', then 'Also worth fixing before launch' and 'Look and feel', which 'can wait'; '## Still needs a person' names 'A pass with a screen reader (VoiceOver or TalkBack)', 'Ten WCAG checks that can't be automated, such as page titles' and 'A short test with about five members on their phones', and the reply lists the assumptions it could not confirm and the out-of-scope bare done page.

mapping.title: Masthead link never reached in Tab walk (loan-open state)
mapping.reason: Settled. The review scopes this item to /tool.html in the 'loan-open' state and cites A11Y-25, the same criterion as F-0141: the link is 'tabbable in the DOM, but a complete Tab walk never reached it'. With the loan-length list open a Tab walk never reaches the header link only because Tab wraps among the options (D09: 'Tab moves to the next option and wraps around'), and the only fix for what the review describes is to let Tab leave the list, which is D09's fix. The sentence 'People who use a keyboard or switch cannot operate it' overstates a link that works in the default state and the severity is inflated, but the reported problem's underlying problem is the seeded trap, and several items may map to one defect.

mapping.title: Basket sessions and find-page search: visual order differs from reading and focus order
mapping.reason: The basket half is D11 exactly: sessions in date order in the DOM, shown in reverse, arrow keys and screen reader running opposite to the screen. The find-page half overlaps D01's focus-order clause; the finding gives most of its weight to the basket reversal, so it maps to D11.

mapping.title: Loan-length button named only by its value
mapping.reason: A screen-reader user tabbing to the control hears only 'One week, collapsed, button' and cannot tell that it sets the loan length; the visible 'Loan length' heading is not part of the name. Not seeded; a genuine accessible-name problem for members using a screen reader.

mapping.title: Session-day button names do not start with the visible '10 Open'
mapping.reason: The name 'Saturday 10 October, open' contains both visible words (10, open) and is more informative than the visible text; a voice-control user can still say the visible digit. No member is hurt; a technical nit rather than a failure.

mapping.title: Session-day dot vanishes in forced colours at 320 px
mapping.reason: At narrow widths the green dot is the only mark that a day is a session, and the forced-colours capture shows it gone while the instruction still says to look for a green dot, so high-contrast users cannot tell open days from closed ones. Distinct from D06 (closed days selectable).

mapping.title: Card and basket item headings at the same level as the section heading
mapping.reason: Tool titles as h2 siblings of the 'Tools' h2 still give a screen-reader user every tool in the heading list; the flat hierarchy does not impede any task. Best-practice nit without demonstrated harm.

mapping.title: Reserve button and status outside any landmark
mapping.reason: The button and status sit between main and contentinfo and are reached by Tab and by linear reading; only landmark-jump navigation skips them and the status is a live region. A best-practice gap with no demonstrated harm to members.

mapping.title: Done page exposes the tool name twice to assistive technology
mapping.reason: Hearing the tool name twice on the confirmation page is a minor redundancy with no effect on understanding or on completing the reservation.

mapping.title: Calendar accepts days when the library is closed
mapping.reason: Any day can be chosen, Monday 12 October is confirmed as 'Pick-up day' without comment, and the basket asks for a session separately; the seeded closed-day defect.

mapping.title: No-results search keeps the previous results and status
mapping.reason: search() returns silently on zero matches so the grid and the status region keep their old content; exactly the seeded empty-search defect, with the same effect for the date and category filters.

mapping.title: Results grid minmax(330px) overflows the 320 px viewport
mapping.reason: The 330 px track minimum against a 288 px content box is the seeded 320 px overflow.

mapping.title: Card names cut to one line, hiding the distinguishing tail
mapping.reason: nowrap plus ellipsis on .card__name hides the 'two batteries' / 'one battery' tail at phone widths; the seeded truncation defect.

mapping.title: Loan-length listbox traps Tab while open
mapping.reason: Tab moves between the options instead of leaving the widget and only Enter closes it; the seeded keyboard trap.

mapping.title: Loan-length listbox stays open on outside click or blur
mapping.reason: A member who taps elsewhere is left with the open list covering the content below it and no way to dismiss it except choosing an option. Adjacent to D09 but about pointer dismissal; fixing it would not remove the keyboard trap, so it is a separate, minor but genuine problem.

mapping.title: Loan-length trigger does not open with ArrowDown or ArrowUp
mapping.reason: Arrow-key opening is an APG convenience; the button still opens with Enter or Space, so no keyboard user is blocked. Claimed from code only, severity 1.

mapping.title: No visible change during the 1.2 s and 1.5 s submit waits
mapping.reason: Only aria-busy is set, with no style, label change or disabled state, so nothing visible says anything is happening while Confirm reservation runs; the no-feedback half of the seeded D12 (the basket Continue uses the same code pattern).

mapping.title: Confirm can be submitted again during the wait, allocating two reservation numbers
mapping.reason: No in-flight guard and the button is not disabled, so a second submit pushes a second reference (FT-4471 and FT-4472); the seeded double-submit defect.

mapping.title: After the hold expires Continue always fails with 'Something went wrong. Try again.'
mapping.reason: The lapsed-hold path shows the generic message and every retry fails the same way; the seeded hold-expiry defect.

mapping.title: 10-minute basket hold never disclosed, warned about or extendable
mapping.reason: The basket says only 'Items are held for you while you finish' with no time shown; the seeded undisclosed-hold defect.

mapping.title: Closed days chosen on the tool page, rejected only after Confirm
mapping.reason: All 21 days are enabled, the closed-day check runs only in the confirm submit, and the error offers no way back to the calendar; the seeded closed-day defect.

mapping.title: 'Change' link drops the chosen session
mapping.reason: The Change link omits the slot parameter, so the basket returns with no session selected and the member must choose again; the seeded defect.

mapping.title: Stated three-tool limit not enforced
mapping.reason: The finder states a three-tool limit but reserve, basket and confirm never check the count, so a member can confirm more tools than allowed and be refused at the desk. Not seeded; a stated rule the system does not enforce.

mapping.title: Phone and membership patterns reject valid formats
mapping.reason: +44 numbers (which autocomplete=tel often supplies), hyphenated or differently spaced numbers and lowercase 'ft-' are rejected, so members with a valid number cannot complete the confirm form without guessing the expected format. Not seeded.

mapping.title: CSS reordering: finder and session list focus order differs from visual order
mapping.reason: The session-list half (row-reverse with wrap-reverse, arrow keys moving opposite to the screen) is D11 verbatim and matches its 2.4.3 criterion; the finder half overlaps D01's focus-order clause. One mapping is required, and the mechanism and criterion match D11.

mapping.title: Dark-mode success token and tint wrong; badge about 3.1:1
mapping.reason: --color-ok #2f7d4a on a tint equal to the surface #1d2622 gives about 3.1:1 for the 'Available from' badge; the seeded dark-theme contrast defect.

mapping.title: 'Added to your basket' toast gone after about 1.35 s with no link
mapping.reason: The toast is the only feedback and disappears in about 1.3 s with no link and nothing persistent; the seeded weak-feedback defect on Reserve.

mapping.title: Fixed action bar covers the end of the page; no space reserved
mapping.reason: position: fixed bar with .page--bar reducing bottom padding to 8 px, so the footer and the last calendar row sit under the bar; the seeded fixed-bar defect.

mapping.title: Search field below the whole tool list on a phone
mapping.reason: At 375 px search and the Filters button come after all ten cards, two-thirds down the page; the seeded phone-layout defect.

mapping.title: Search results update above the viewport
mapping.reason: Because the search box sits below the list on phones, the filtered results and the '2 tools found' status change out of view; a consequence of the same layout reordering as D01, which its fix removes.

mapping.title: Day grid below the fold, heading under the sticky bar, commit button offered first
mapping.reason: A fixed bar covers whatever lies at the fold until the member scrolls, and a required choice below the first viewport on a 375 px phone with an always-visible CTA is the ordinary mobile pattern; the finding does not show that pressing Reserve without a day fails. Speculative.

mapping.title: After Reserve nothing persistent says the reservation is unfinished
mapping.reason: Only the short toast, the button label unchanged, and 'Basket (1)' scrolled out of view at 375 px; the seeded defect.

mapping.title: Basket asks for a pick-up session again with nothing preselected
mapping.reason: The day chosen on the tool page is repeated on the basket card but not carried into the session list, so the member answers the same question twice and can pick a contradicting session. Not one of the seeded defects (D13 is the Change round trip).

mapping.title: Sessions listed latest first
mapping.reason: Wed 28 first and Sat 10 last, so the first Saturday shown is not this Saturday; the visual face of the seeded reversed session layout.

mapping.title: Continue and Confirm give no acknowledgement
mapping.reason: Screen unchanged for about a second after the tap with no pressed or busy state; the no-feedback half of the seeded D12.

mapping.title: No-match search shows the full list and no message
mapping.reason: 'sewing machine' leaves all ten tools on screen and the status empty; the seeded defect.

mapping.title: Filters toggle is icon-only
mapping.reason: The three-line icon button with no visible text is the only way to the date and category filters; named in D01's description.

mapping.title: 'Available from' filter hint does not match its behaviour
mapping.reason: The hint promises tools you could pick up on or after the entered day, but entering 12 October removes tools available from 14, 17, 21 and 24 October, so a member planning a later Saturday is wrongly shown fewer tools. Label and behaviour disagree; not seeded.

mapping.title: Pick-up dates before the tool is available are accepted
mapping.reason: A tool available from 17 October can be reserved for 10 October and every session is offered, so a member can book a collection before the tool is back and find nothing to collect. Distinct from D06 (closed days).

mapping.title: Pick-up day and pick-up session can contradict each other
mapping.reason: The confirm page can show 'pick up Saturday 17 October' beside 'Pick-up session Wednesday 21 October', so the member does not know when to collect and the desk holds two dates. Not seeded; a genuine flow-consistency problem.

mapping.title: Typed confirm details lost after Change
mapping.reason: Using Change, choosing a session and continuing returns to an empty membership field, so the member must retype within the same reservation. Different data and cause from D13 (session not preselected).

mapping.title: Remove is immediate with no undo
mapping.reason: Immediate removal with an empty-basket message is the normal basket pattern; the member explicitly pressed Remove and recovery is a few taps. Undo is a preference, not a demonstrated harm.

mapping.title: Error summary stays after the basket is emptied
mapping.reason: After a failed Continue and then Remove, the page says the basket is empty while the 'There is a problem' alert still asks to choose a session and links to a list that no longer exists; a stale, misleading error. Minor but a real state bug.

mapping.title: Basket does not say how long tools are held
mapping.reason: 'Items are held for you while you finish' with no duration; the seeded undisclosed-hold defect.

mapping.title: Reserved tool stays in the basket after confirmation
mapping.reason: After confirming, 'Basket (1)' and a basket still showing the drill with a Continue button suggest the tool is not yet reserved, inviting a second reservation or confusion at the desk. Not seeded.

mapping.title: Format errors read like empty-field errors
mapping.reason: Both messages give the expected format ('like FT-01234', 'like 07700 900123'), which is an adequate suggestion for the typed value; distinguishing 'empty' from 'wrong format' is polish.

mapping.title: Loan-length list does not close with Escape
mapping.reason: Escape leaves the list open; part of the seeded listbox trap ('Escape does nothing').

mapping.title: Search and filter state not kept in the URL
mapping.reason: Bookmarking or reloading a filtered list of ten tools is not a need of members reserving a tool; a nicety, severity 1.

mapping.title: Change opens the basket with no session selected
mapping.reason: Arriving from Change with Saturday 17 October chosen, no radio is checked; the seeded defect.

mapping.title: Calendar-day focus hidden under the sticky Reserve bar
mapping.reason: Tab reaches Friday 16 / Saturday 24 October but the fixed bar covers the focused button completely; the seeded fixed-bar focus defect.

mapping.title: Every calendar day is a tab stop; over 20 presses to reach Reserve
mapping.reason: Settled. The review measures a concrete cost, not a preference: 'every one of the 21 day buttons is in the tab order: eight Tabs from Loan length only reach Friday 16 October, sixteen reach Saturday 24 October, and the Reserve button comes after all 21'. For keyboard and switch members that is over twenty presses on every tool page before the primary action, on the critical path of the flow. It fits none of the not-a-problem kinds (not wrong, not speculative, not taste), and no seeded defect covers it (D08 is the bar hiding focus, not the number of stops). Consistent with the agreed real-unseeded mappings of F-0029 and F-0031, moderate accessibility costs with a demonstrated effect, and unlike F-0143, where Enter and Space still work at no cost.

mapping.title: Same placeholder wrench thumbnail on every card
mapping.reason: Look and feel: the thumbnail carries no information, but the name, category and availability do; a matter of appeal, not a usability problem for reserving a tool.

mapping.title: No identity beyond the name in the masthead
mapping.reason: Brand and visual identity; a matter of taste, not a usability or accessibility problem.

mapping.title: Sticky Reserve bar hides the open loan-length options at 375 px
mapping.reason: Settled. The review's words are 'the fixed Reserve bar covers every option except One week' at 375 px on /tool.html, under A11Y-05, and its reply files this under one problem: 'The sticky Reserve this tool bar on phones hides what sits under it... It covers keyboard focus on calendar days and on the loan-length button, and covers the open loan-length options at 375 px.' That is D08's underlying problem on the same page: the bar 'is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it', so it covers interactive content, including the focused option as a member arrows down the list. Both graders already mapped F-0025 (the same control's focused button hidden behind the bar) and F-0097 to D08; the open list of that button is the same defect, not a new one. Which CSS fix the author would pick does not change the underlying problem.

mapping.title: Added-to-basket toast drawn over calendar cells
mapping.reason: A toast overlaying content for about a second is its normal behaviour; no harm shown.

mapping.title: Tool names truncated at 375 px so the drills look identical
mapping.reason: 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' for both drills; the seeded truncation defect.

mapping.title: Native date and select controls, misaligned
mapping.reason: Native pickers are usable (and often better on phones); a ~30 px label offset is visual polish, not a usability problem.

mapping.title: Dark theme drops the available badge's pill
mapping.reason: The missing tint is the seeded dark-mode badge problem seen from the design side: the tint equals the card surface, leaving green text on the card at about 3.1:1.

mapping.title: Reservation number, session and deposit without emphasis on the done page
mapping.reason: The values are present and labelled in the summary box; emphasis is hierarchy polish, not a usability problem.

mapping.title: Sessions latest-first in an uneven one-plus-five layout at desktop
mapping.reason: The backwards order and the stranded full-width card are the row-reverse / wrap-reverse layout seeded as D11.

mapping.title: Two detail lists with misaligned value columns
mapping.reason: A 44 px difference between value columns is visual polish; the details remain readable.

mapping.title: Search below the whole tool list on phones
mapping.reason: Search and the filter button after all ten cards at 375 px; the seeded defect.

mapping.title: No visual identity beyond the name
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0111; brand taste, not usability.

mapping.title: Reservation number shares the FT- prefix with membership numbers
mapping.reason: Confusion between FT-4471 and FT-01234 is speculative; the two differ in length and are labelled where shown.

mapping.title: Same wrench glyph on every card
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0110; appeal, not usability.

mapping.title: No identity or focal point on any surface
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0111; taste.

mapping.title: Titles truncate on phones so the two drills read identically
mapping.reason: The same seeded truncation.

mapping.title: Search block below all ten cards on phones
mapping.reason: The same seeded phone layout.

mapping.title: Unthemed browser-default date and select controls
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0114; polish.

mapping.title: Two misaligned definition lists under Details
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0118; polish.

mapping.title: Sessions in reverse date order with a stranded full-width card
mapping.reason: The same reversed layout.

mapping.title: Right half of the page empty at 1280 px
mapping.reason: A ~610 px reading column on a wide screen is a normal measure; taste.

mapping.title: Footer stops short, grey band below
mapping.reason: Cosmetic on short pages at 1280 x 900; no effect on members.

mapping.title: Done page still shows 'Basket (1)'
mapping.reason: Same genuine problem as F-0080: after confirmation the header implies the tool is still unreserved in the basket.

mapping.title: Available badges lose their tint in dark mode
mapping.reason: The same seeded dark-mode badge problem as F-0115 and F-0050.

mapping.title: No-results search shows the full catalogue on phones
mapping.reason: The same seeded empty-search defect.

mapping.title: 'Oct' wraps alone in badges at 375 px
mapping.reason: Typographic polish; 'Available from Sat 10 / Oct' is still readable.

mapping.title: Navigation links wrap to two lines at 375 px
mapping.reason: The links remain legible and tappable; a taller masthead is polish.

mapping.title: Confirm and done fill only half the width at 1280 px
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0148; taste.

mapping.title: Reservation number is plain body text
mapping.reason: Duplicate of F-0146; polish.

mapping.title: No-results state shows the full list with no empty-state message
mapping.reason: The same seeded defect, stated from the design side with a capture caveat.

mapping.title: axe colour contrast 3.07:1, #2f7d4a on #1d2622
mapping.reason: The seeded dark-theme badge contrast, found by axe.

mapping.title: 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' at 3.07:1 in the dark theme
mapping.reason: The seeded dark-theme badge contrast, found by the contrast check.

mapping.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: 'Members can reserve up to three tools at'
mapping.reason: Advisory only: passes WCAG at 8.33:1; no member is hurt by text at that contrast.

mapping.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: 'Category'
mapping.reason: Advisory only: passes WCAG at 8.33:1.

mapping.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: 'Items are held for you while you finish.'
mapping.reason: Advisory only: passes WCAG at 8.33:1.

mapping.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: 'Tools'
mapping.reason: Advisory only: passes WCAG at 7.33:1.

mapping.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: 'Reservation number'
mapping.reason: Advisory only: passes WCAG at 7.33:1.

mapping.title: Day button and Reserve bar 0 px apart at 768 px
mapping.reason: The zero gap is the fixed bar lying over the first calendar rows at 768 px, which D08 describes.

mapping.title: Card h2 clips under the text-spacing override
mapping.reason: The nowrap / overflow-hidden name truncation seeded as D03, surfaced by the 1.4.12 override.

mapping.title: Card h2 clips at 200 % text size
mapping.reason: The same one-line name truncation under zoom.

mapping.title: #reserve overlaps day '17' at 1280 px
mapping.reason: D08 names the third calendar row sitting under the bar at 1280 px.

mapping.title: Horizontal page overflow 346 px > 320 px
mapping.reason: The seeded 26 px sideways scroll at 320 px from the results list items.

mapping.title: Content does not reflow at 320 px
mapping.reason: The same seeded overflow reported against 1.4.10.

mapping.title: Card h2 clipped at 320 px (327 vs 184 px)
mapping.reason: The same one-line name truncation at phone width.

mapping.title: #reserve overlaps #tool-from under the spacing override at 320 px
mapping.reason: Settled. The finding says only that 'At 320 px with the WCAG 1.4.12 spacing override, #reserve (Reserve this tool) overlaps #tool-from (Saturday 10 October)': a static detail line in the upper part of the tool page that happens to sit in the bottom 72 px of the first viewport once the override lengthens the page. A fixed bar always paints over whatever is at the fold, and the line scrolls into view, so nothing is lost under the override and no 1.4.12 failure is shown. D08's harm is different (the page ending 8 px under the calendar so the footer runs under the bar, and focused day buttons covered); D08's fix would not change this overlap and removing this overlap would not fix D08. Both graders agreed that F-0060, 'a fixed bar covers whatever lies at the fold until the member scrolls', is not-a-problem, and the same reasoning applies here. A checker artefact.

mapping.title: #reserve overlaps #tool-blurb at 200 % text size
mapping.reason: Settled. The same artefact as F-0015 at 200 % text size: 'At 320 px with the root font size at 200 %, #reserve (Reserve this tool) overlaps #tool-blurb (A brushless combi drill with hammer action...)'. The blurb is the description paragraph near the top of the page; at 200 % it reaches the fold at scroll 0 and the fixed bar paints over its last lines until the member scrolls. No content or function is lost, so it is not a 1.4.4 failure, and it is neither D08's end-of-page coverage nor its focused-control coverage. Consistent with the agreed not-a-problem mapping of F-0060.

mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'You can collect at any of these sessions'
mapping.reason: A typographic widow; no effect on members.

mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'Nothing is paid online...'
mapping.reason: A typographic widow; no effect on members.

mapping.title: Body text 9.7 px from the right edge at 320 px
mapping.reason: The 330 px card overflowing a 320 px viewport pushes its text to the edge; the same cause as D05.

mapping.title: One word on the last line: tool heading at 320 px
mapping.reason: A typographic widow; no effect on members.

mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'Reservation confirmed'
mapping.reason: A typographic widow; no effect on members.

mapping.title: Cramped padding 6.4 px in the card body
mapping.reason: A 2 px shortfall in card padding is polish.

mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'Drills and drivers · deposit £20'
mapping.reason: A typographic widow; no effect on members.

mapping.title: Focus jumps back from the tile saw to 'Search tools'
mapping.reason: Focus order running against the visual order on the finder is the focus clause of D01.

mapping.title: Focused 'One week' hidden behind the action bar
mapping.reason: The fixed bar covering a focused control; the seeded D08 mechanism, here on the loan-length button.

settled.reason: Grader A's mapping. The review scopes the item to /tool.html in the 'loan-open' state and cites A11Y-25, the criterion of the trap finding F-0141: the link is 'tabbable in the DOM, but a complete Tab walk never reached it'. With the loan-length list open, a Tab walk never reaches the header link only because Tab wraps among the options, which is D09 ('Tab moves to the next option and wraps around... a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter'); the only fix for what the review describes is to let Tab leave the list, D09's fix. The reported problem is therefore the same underlying problem as D09, and the mapping instructions allow several items per defect, so F-0141 does not exclude it. Grader B is right that 'People who use a keyboard or switch cannot operate it' overstates a link that works in the default state and that severity 4 is inflated, but within the stated state the observation is true, so it is not 'wrong' in the not-a-problem sense; mapping a symptom to its seeded cause is also how both graders treated F-0058 (D01), F-0019 (D05) and F-0008 (D08).

Grader A's mapping. The review measures a concrete, repeated cost rather than stating a preference: 'every one of the 21 day buttons is in the tab order: eight Tabs from Loan length only reach Friday 16 October, sixteen reach Saturday 24 October, and the Reserve button comes after all 21'. For keyboard and switch members that is over twenty presses on every tool page before the primary action, on the critical path of the reservation, and it is what walks them through the focus D08 hides. It fits none of the not-a-problem kinds in the mapping instructions (not wrong, not speculative, not a matter of taste, not a positive remark), and no seeded defect covers it: D08 is the bar hiding focus, not the number of stops. This is consistent with the agreed real-unseeded mappings of F-0029 and F-0031 (moderate accessibility costs with a demonstrated effect) and different from the agreed not-a-problem F-0143, where Enter and Space still open the list at no cost.

Grader A's mapping. The review's words are 'At 375 px, with the loan-length list opened, the fixed Reserve bar covers every option except One week', under A11Y-05, and the reply itself files it as one problem with the focus items: 'The sticky Reserve this tool bar on phones hides what sits under it. It covers keyboard focus on calendar days and on the loan-length button, and covers the open loan-length options at 375 px.' D08 is that bar: 'fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it', covering interactive content on the same page, including the focused option when a member arrows down the open list (D08's criterion is 2.4.11, focus not obscured). Both graders already mapped F-0025, the same control's focused button hidden behind the bar, and F-0097 to D08; the open list of that same button is the same underlying problem, not a new one. Grader B's point that the author might fix it with stacking or a flip rather than page padding is about the remedy, not the underlying problem, which is what the mapping instructions ask about.

Grader B's mapping. The finding states only that 'At 320 px with the WCAG 1.4.12 spacing override, #reserve (Reserve this tool) overlaps #tool-from (Saturday 10 October)'. #tool-from is a static detail line in the upper part of the tool page that happens to land in the bottom 72 px of the first viewport once the override lengthens the page; a fixed bar always paints over whatever sits at the fold at scroll 0, and the line scrolls into view, so nothing is lost under the override and no 1.4.12 failure is shown. D08's harm is elsewhere: the page ending 8 px under the calendar so the footer runs under the bar, and focused day buttons being covered; a D08 fix would not change this overlap, and removing this overlap would not fix D08, so it is not 'the same underlying problem'. Both graders agreed that F-0060 ('A fixed bar covers whatever lies at the fold until the member scrolls') is not-a-problem, and consistency requires the same here. A checker artefact of the fixed bar, not a defect.

Grader B's mapping, for the same reason as F-0015. The finding says 'At 320 px with the root font size at 200 %, #reserve (Reserve this tool) overlaps #tool-blurb (A brushless combi drill with hammer action...)': the description paragraph near the top of the tool page, which at 200 % reaches the fold at scroll 0 so the fixed bar paints over its last lines until the member scrolls. No content or function is lost, so it is not a 1.4.4 failure, and it is neither D08's end-of-page coverage nor its focused-control coverage. Consistent with the agreed not-a-problem mapping of F-0060.
